chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn al-Numan from Hammad ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man asks me to bear witness for him in a testimony, and I know his handwriting and his seal, but I remember little or much of the rest. He said to me: 'If your companion is trustworthy and there is with him another trustworthy man, then bear witness for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a witness to testify on behalf of someone based on knowing their handwriting and seal?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the evidentiary standards for written contracts, permitting a single witness to testify if they recognize the signer's handwriting and seal, provided the signer is trustworthy and accompanied by another reliable individual. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the integrity (*thiqa*) of parties and the practical utility of documentary evidence in civil transactions, bridging the gap between oral testimony and written records.
